purpose: renderer-neutral visual-story strategy, semantic content-role, asset-implication, and layout/shot-shape candidates for Storyboard Enhance

blueprints.name: Agent Progress Theater
best: machine/agent work must be visible over time
progress, scan, build, processing, checklist, message-thread receipt
state mutation is the proof
avoid: the main action is typing a prompt
a user cursor must drive every UI state
a static list is enough
requires: at least one meaningful working state
a visible result or state change
blueprints.shape: trigger → visible work-in-progress → result materializes → result resolves or remains partially active
blueprints.story_job: Make intermediate working states and their mutation into a receipt/result the evidence of a multi-step process.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Camera Journey
best: cause and consequence live in different regions of one continuous world
travel itself explains the relationship
the scene benefits from scale/depth/spatial discovery
avoid: one object or device is the only hero
the camera would move without narrative reason
a simple cut communicates the relation better
requires: at least two meaningful destinations or phases
blueprints.shape: enter world → travel to first focus → event/meaning fires → travel to consequence → settle
blueprints.story_job: Use one continuous world where moving from an initiating action or detail to its consequence is itself part of the explanation.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Balanced Comparison
best: exactly two concepts/assets/states have equal weight
the viewer must compare them at the same time
symmetry clarifies the claim
avoid: more than two primary items
one side is clearly subordinate
the comparison is mainly temporal and should be shown sequentially
blueprints.shape: comparison premise → paired subjects establish → differences/similarities become legible → balanced hold or decisive emphasis
blueprints.story_job: Put exactly two semantically comparable subjects into one common frame of reference so their difference or complementarity can be inspected.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Hub and Satellites
best: one core connects many peers
ecosystem/integration/central-platform relationships
the center must become the final focus
avoid: relationships are sequential rather than radial
there is no meaningful central entity
many nodes would become unreadable
blueprints.shape: satellites establish around hub → relation becomes obvious → converge, orbit, or focus toward hub → hold on core
blueprints.story_job: Show one anchor as the organizing center of multiple related peers or dependencies.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Identity to Action Morph
best: one identity/state should become one action at the same focal anchor
the scene needs a compact final action beat
a transformation is clearer than introducing a new layout
avoid: multiple actions compete
the CTA requires a multi-step workflow
there is no meaningful shared identity between before and after
blueprints.shape: identity/focal object holds → transforms in place → action becomes clear → optional interaction confirms → hold
blueprints.story_job: Concentrate attention on one identity/widget that changes into one actionable state and, when appropriate, receives a single confirming interaction.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Interaction-Driven Surface Demo
best: a visible user interaction is the causal actor
a real interface/workflow is the evidence
2–4 discrete interaction states tell the story
avoid: the machine acts after one trigger without continued user input
the scene is only a static product showcase
the interface can be summarized more clearly without simulated interaction
requires: an interaction sequence with causal changes
blueprints.shape: surface establish → interaction → state response → next interaction/state → payoff
blueprints.story_job: Explain a real interactive workflow by making user actions visibly cause state changes on the same product surface.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire truthful source media/capture for the primary evidence role before layout.

blueprints.name: Data Hero / Metric Journey
best: numbers/charts are the evidence
one metric or trend should dominate
the argument depends on quantitative change
avoid: data is decorative or unsupported
multiple unrelated metrics compete
a narrative asset is more important than the numbers
blueprints.shape: data instrument establishes → values/trend develop → supporting metrics recede → hero metric lands
blueprints.story_job: Let verified quantitative evidence carry the argument through one or more data states, then land on the metric or relationship that matters.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Surface Hero Showcase
best: a product/page/device surface itself is the evidence
the viewer should experience a feature within one persistent surface
screen state changes are more important than pointer choreography
avoid: the camera must traverse many unrelated regions
a cursor-driven workflow is the primary story
the scene has no real surface to showcase
requires: at least one meaningful state change or internal flow
blueprints.shape: surface establishes as hero → internal state/flow advances → focal feature is emphasized → surface settles
blueprints.story_job: Hold one product/device/surface as the hero while its real states or views demonstrate the core experience.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire truthful source media/capture for the primary evidence role before layout.

blueprints.name: Fixed Anchor, Cycling World
best: one identity/statement must stay constant while surrounding examples vary
breadth is the claim
repetition around a stable anchor communicates consistency
avoid: the anchor itself must transform
items need simultaneous comparison
the cycle would become filler rather than evidence
blueprints.shape: anchor establishes → surrounding states cycle → cadence may change → final state joins/resolves with anchor
blueprints.story_job: Keep one semantic anchor constant while a peer slot or surrounding state cycles, proving breadth or variation without losing identity.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Collection Assemble
best: many peers must accumulate into one collection
breadth/coverage is the point
the viewer benefits from seeing the set co-resident at the end
avoid: only two items need comparison
items have a strict causal sequence
collection density would exceed readability
blueprints.shape: empty/partial field → items arrive progressively → collection structure becomes clear → assembled set holds or reframes
blueprints.story_job: Reveal a peer collection whose breadth or accumulation is the evidence, without requiring literal cards.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Kinetic Type Beats
best: words/phrases themselves carry the argument
a hook or payoff can be expressed through changing language
minimal imagery is intentional
avoid: visual evidence is required
the scene would become a generic text slideshow
too much copy must be read at once
blueprints.shape: text premise → token/phrase change or escalating beats → emphasis/payoff → hold or handoff
blueprints.story_job: Let wording itself carry the scene through successive statement states; use when the semantic evidence is primarily language rather than external media.
blueprints.asset_hint: Prefer text/data/generated graphics; do not fetch media just to fill space.

blueprints.name: Identity Assemble to Lockup
best: a mark/identity must come into existence or resolve from prior material
brand/product identity is the semantic payoff
parts-to-whole transformation is meaningful
avoid: there is no meaningful identity object
the scene needs factual evidence more than branding
assembly would be decorative filler
requires: a justified source state: parts, prior phrase, marks, or cleared field
blueprints.shape: prepare/clear → parts or prior material transform toward identity → lockup completes → hold or extend to CTA
blueprints.story_job: Make one identity/mark come into existence or resolve from prior material, then hold it as the semantic conclusion.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Accumulation to Overwhelm
best: the problem is too many tools/windows/alerts/items
density itself is evidence
the emotional arc should move from recognition to pressure
avoid: the problem is quantitative rather than experiential
many items would be fabricated rather than sourced
the viewer needs calm comparison rather than overload
requires: one focal victim/subject or central question
blueprints.shape: normal field → elements accumulate → density crosses threshold → focal subject becomes surrounded or center opens for the question
blueprints.story_job: Make accumulation itself the evidence that a focal subject is becoming overloaded or surrounded.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Coupled Control and Result
best: one control change must visibly cause another surface to update
cause and effect must be seen simultaneously
editing/inspection is the feature
avoid: the workflow is click-through rather than continuous manipulation
the result can appear after a cut with no loss of meaning
the two surfaces cannot fit readably together
blueprints.shape: coupled regions establish → control changes → result responds in same beat → repeat/refine → final result demonstrates edited behavior
blueprints.story_job: Keep a control/input and its target/result visible as one causal pair so changes can be inspected in the same beat.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Prompt to Generated Result
best: a typed ask is causally important
the machine response is the payoff
AI/search/command behavior must be demonstrated
avoid: typing is just decorative text
the user must keep clicking through a workflow
the output has no credible surface or artifact
blueprints.shape: input surface establishes → prompt types → submit/commit → machine works/responds → result lands or loop restarts
blueprints.story_job: Make a meaningful input causally produce an observable machine response, so the ask→answer relationship is the scene.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Spatial Stations
best: milestones/steps/concepts can live at distinct spatial stations
sequence and location should reinforce each other
one canvas can hold the whole path
avoid: the sequence has no spatial meaning
camera travel would be longer than the content warrants
the items need simultaneous comparison
blueprints.shape: wide spatial map implied → station 1 focus → travel → station 2 focus → … → final station hold
blueprints.story_job: Turn an ordered set of milestones, concepts, or evidence points into distinct stations in one coherent conceptual world.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Cycle then Takeover
best: several possibilities should be rejected/replaced by one decisive hero
the final reveal should feel physically dominant
a collision/takeover communicates the rhetorical turn
avoid: the transition should be calm
the alternatives are evidence that must remain visible
the hero does not semantically replace the earlier options
blueprints.shape: context establishes → options cycle → hero enters with force → prior content yields/exits → hero holds
blueprints.story_job: Cycle through plausible alternatives, then replace them with one semantically decisive hero that resolves the uncertainty.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Quiet Landing / Title Reveal
best: the video needs a breather or landing beat
one short title/proof/identity statement deserves stillness
low motion is intentionally contrasted with busy neighbors
avoid: multiple ideas must develop
a static card would hide a required visual progression
low motion is being used only because implementation is easier
requires: one concise dominant message or proof
blueprints.shape: clean field establishes → one restrained reveal/change → still readable hold
blueprints.story_job: Give one short semantic message enough visual stillness to land between denser scenes.
blueprints.asset_hint: Prefer text/data/generated graphics; do not fetch media just to fill space.

blueprints.name: Long Surface to Artifact Reveal
best: a long transcript/feed/document is evidence of work
traversal demonstrates quantity or process
one artifact/detail should emerge as payoff
avoid: there is no meaningful long surface
scrolling would be unreadable filler
the artifact can be shown directly without losing the proof
requires: one focal pivot into an artifact/detail
blueprints.shape: long surface establishes → traverse meaningful excerpts → focal item selected/highlighted → artifact/detail expands or replaces field → payoff hold
blueprints.story_job: Use a long evidence surface to prove work/quantity/process, then pivot from one selected part into the concrete artifact or detail it produced.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Typewriter Reveal
best: the act of typing is itself relatable or meaningful
one line should feel authored live
typed text should transform into or support a payoff
avoid: typing only slows down information
the scene needs a real product input and machine response
copy is too long for readable live typing
requires: short text suitable for live reveal
blueprints.shape: caret/typing begins → line completes or edits → line collapses/yields or remains as anchor → payoff appears → hold
blueprints.story_job: Make the act of authoring one short line the evidence, then let that line resolve into a semantic payoff or identity.
blueprints.asset_hint: Prefer text/data/generated graphics; do not fetch media just to fill space.

blueprints.name: Media to Text Handoff
best: a video/image/demo should yield to a metric or statement without disappearing immediately
show → impact → interpretation is the rhetorical arc
the same visual weight should transfer across media types
avoid: the media and text have no causal relation
a clean cut is semantically stronger
screen space cannot support a readable overlap/handoff
requires: one metric/text payoff related to that media
blueprints.shape: media establishes → media yields space while staying present → metric/result inherits weight → media clears → text/statement takes center → final stamp
blueprints.story_job: Let primary media establish evidence, then transfer visual importance to the metric or statement that interprets that evidence.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire truthful source media/capture for the primary evidence role before layout.

blueprints.name: Nested Zoom-Out Reveal
best: a close-up detail gains new meaning when revealed inside a larger whole
scale/context reversal is the payoff
one continuous outward reveal is stronger than cuts
avoid: there is no genuine containing whole
the scene needs several unrelated camera legs
zoom-out is being used only for spectacle
blueprints.shape: tight detail → local action → continuous outward reveal through context layers → wide containing whole → wide-frame payoff
blueprints.story_job: Start from one meaningful detail and reveal that it belongs to a larger containing system without breaking identity.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Interruption and Re-entry
best: one continuous process is interrupted and later resumed
the unfinished state must survive the interruption
re-entry/context reconstruction is the semantic point
avoid: generic overload is the main claim
the interruption permanently replaces the original process
a simple before/after comparison is enough
requires: a distinct re-entry or reconstruction phase
blueprints.shape: active process → interruption → unfinished state preserved → return without full context → reconstruction → same process resumes
blueprints.story_job: Keep one process identifiable across interruption, incomplete return, context reconstruction, and resumption so re-entry cost is visible.
blueprints.asset_hint: Acquire external media only when it materially strengthens a required semantic role.

blueprints.name: Abstract to Concrete Timeline
best: an abstract duration/timeline becomes a concrete schedule or calendar
temporal landmarks must survive a change of representation
the concrete surface should inherit identity from the abstract model
avoid: the concrete example is unrelated to the abstract model
there is no representation change
the scene is primarily a simultaneous comparison
requires: shared duration, order, landmarks, or state identity
blueprints.shape: abstract time model → invariant landmarks → added real-world context → concrete schedule resolves → inherited identity holds
blueprints.story_job: Transform an abstract time/order model into a concrete schedule/example while visibly preserving the same duration, landmarks, order, or state identity.
blueprints.asset_hint: Prefer text/data/generated graphics; do not fetch media just to fill space.
